title: Littlewild · Shape, expression and craft
intent: The second artboard fidelity pass. Compare the supplied designs with actual editable 3D characters, identify remaining differences, and retain the authoring and review evidence. Tests establish contracts; these images establish what was actually rendered.

sections.title: The supplied target and the new character
sections.intent: A warm woodland companion: expressive eyes, a sculpted jaw, distinct legs, a fitted cap and draped cape.

cards.title: Supplied clothed concept
cards.caption: Page 1 of the supplied high-fidelity mockups. Design target, not implemented software.

cards.title: Actual revised character · three-quarter view
cards.caption: Real revision-4 geometry rendered from the retained recipe. The recipe selects a rain cape to match the concept’s shoulder garment and the warm Honey coat.

cards.title: Previous revision
cards.caption: The previous accepted implementation. Different camera and clothing settings; this is a visual history, not a pixel-difference test.

cards.title: Supplied shape and coat target
cards.caption: Page 9 clarifies the jaw, legs, eye treatment and coat direction without the outfit.

cards.title: Actual revised body
cards.caption: Actual bare model with distinct legs, inset eyes, shaped jaw and bounded short-fibre geometry. Surface detail and portable geometry remain editable data.

sections.title: The dedicated editor
sections.intent: Keep the real exported model at the center of the UI, with usable desktop and mobile controls.

cards.title: Desktop editor
cards.caption: The actual running editor with the new companion, warmer light and repeatable three-quarter camera.

cards.title: Mobile editor
cards.caption: The same editor and recipe at 390 px; no separate illustration or mobile-only model.

sections.title: Inspect the silhouette and attachments
sections.intent: Neutral views and explicit animation phases expose defects a hero frame can conceal.

cards.title: Studio · repeatable multiview review
cards.caption: Front, three-quarter, side, back, portrait and world lighting. The retained plan also captures walking and working at explicit times, so agents can repeat the same pose.

cards.title: Forge · the same exported companion
cards.caption: Authored meshes, UVs and versioned textures preserved through the Forge import. See the export receipt for GLB validation; renderer lighting differs.

cards.title: Actual native Godot capture
cards.caption: The final visual rendered through the actual native asset factory with baked versioned textures. The receipt binds the visual, image, factory and capture script.

sections.title: Author, compare and maintain with agents
sections.intent: Discover capabilities; perform guarded changes; retain exact source and camera inputs; compare actual captures.

cards.title: Three executable maintenance workflow
cards.caption: Executed public-CLI lifecycle with exact binary hashes, guarded dry runs, eight textured GLBs, native rig and gameplay preservation, and engine re-export.

cards.title: Maintain the dressed character
cards.caption: The actual cap/cape/satchel/boots character refined in Forge and reattached to the engine. Exact unchanged mesh buffers are reused, all variants and gameplay remain intact, and the existing geometry budget stays enforced.

cards.title: Engine · installed character facts
cards.caption: Actual read-only inspection of the installed engine character: project fingerprint, variant materials, surface versions, mesh counts and UV coverage.

cards.title: Forge silhouette profiles
cards.caption: Executed bounded organic-profile authoring through the CLI. Stations control width, depth and offset along the height; the mesh remains portable through native assets and GLB.

cards.title: Remaining visual differences
cards.caption: The result is a portable stylized 3D companion. Short geometric fibres and texture maps are not a strand-hair simulation; eyes and gaze remain simpler, the cape is more rigid, and materials, lighting and scenery still differ from the illustration. Native and browser renderers are not pixel-identical. Judge fidelity from these real frames rather than passing contract tests.
